newsitem.title: USA: Supplement to Harris Cty, Texas MUD 10 and 350 POS.
newsitem.headline: Supplement to Harris Cty, Texas MUD 10 and 350 POS.

text.p: Supplement to Preliminary Official Statement Dated November 22, 1996 Relating to Harris Cty Municipal Utility District No. 350 Unlimited Tax Bonds, Series 1996 and Supplement to Preliminary Official Statement Dated November 22, 1996 Relating to Harris Cty Municipal Utility District No. 10 Waterworks and Sewer System Unlimited Tax bonds, Series 1996 The Preliminary Official Statements related to the above referenced bonds are hereby supplemented as follows. As stated in each Preliminary Official Statement, the City of Houston has initiated proceedings to annex all of the territory within Kingwood and to dissolve the thirteen water disticts (the "Kingwood Districts") located there, including Harris County Municipal Utility District No. 350 and Harris County Municipal Utility District No. 10 (the "Districts"), which proceedings are subject to a number of contingencies and are being contasted vigorously in litigation filed by the Kingwood Districts and others. On November 27, 1996, representatives of the City and the Kingwood Districts (including the Districts) engaged attorneys to determine whether a possible agreement between the City and Harris County Utility District No. 5, the district which is wholesale provider of water in Kingwood ("No. 5"), would be enforeable. Under the terms of the possible agreement, No. 5 would pay the City periodic fee for water used for an initial term of 10 years, which fee would have to be refunded if the City intiated proceedings to annex Kingwood. It is anticipated that any charge No. 5 might agree to pay to the City would be passed on to all purchasers of water from No. 5, including the Districts, and could multiply their costs of wholesale water supply aby as much as 150% to 300%. The Districts are unable to predict whether such an agreement will be finally negotiated by presentatives of the City and the Kingwood Districts or whether the agreement would be approved by the City Council of Houston and all of the governing boards of the Kingwood Districts or what financial impact of such an agreement of each of the Districts would be. The Districts anticipate that if such an agreement is approved by all necessary parties. annexation of the Districts by the City of Houston would be deferred for an extended term of years. As noted in the Preliminary Official Statements, no prospective purchaser of the bonds being offered by Harris County Municipal Utility District No. 350 or Harris County Municipal Utility District No. 10 should assume that the City of Houston will be responsible for payment of the bonds described in the Preliminary Official Statements. The date of this Supplement is December 2, 1996.
